slop_types: a quiet week padded into seven sections
says-nothing summary ('steady, consistent results', 'demonstrating the continued effectiveness of our current strategy', 'healthy and well-balanced account')
'deep dive' and 'insights' headings over routine numbers
tiny moves narrated as findings (mobile share 'slight increase', Wednesday 'slight dip')
punts posing as recommendations ('continue monitoring', 'keep an eye on', 'explore opportunities to further optimize')

planted_traps.why: nothing moved enough to act on; the rewrite should say so in one line, give 2-4 numbers and the next date, and stop
a rate change on 6 purchases is noise and must not survive as a finding

planted_traps.where: Saturday's 34 purchases 'could potentially indicate shifting weekend shopping behavior'
planted_traps.why: one week of day-of-week data supports no pattern

expected_watchouts.where: tablet conversion rate 1.9% vs 2.4% on 6 purchases
expected_watchouts.why: below any sample floor for a rate claim; flagged 'may warrant further attention' anyway
a behavioral claim from a single Saturday

cut_list: executive summary and closing line (no content)
revenue and CPA (ROAS and purchases already carry them)
device insights, including the 6-purchase tablet rate
notes: Synthetic coffee-subscription store. The quiet-week gold follows the research format: one line saying it's on track and nothing needs action, four numbers, the next date, a Basis line. ROAS 4.12 = $21,590 / $5,240; campaign purchases sum to 188. The gold is at the 25% floor on purpose: a quiet week should come out as short as the ratio allows.
